title: Circadian transcriptome of pancreatic adenocarcinoma unravels chronotherapeutic targets.
summary: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDA) is a lethal cancer characterized by a poor outcome and an increasing incidence. A significant majority (>80%) of newly diagnosed cases are deemed unresectable, leaving chemotherapy as the sole viable option, though with only moderate success. This necessitates the identification of improved therapeutic options for PDA. We hypothesized that there are temporal variations in cancer-relevant processes within PDA tumors, offering insights into the optimal timing of drug administration—a concept termed chronotherapy. In this study, we explored the presence of the circadian transcriptome in PDA using patient-derived organoids (PDOs) and validated these findings by comparing PDA data from TCGA with non-cancerous healthy pancreas data from GTeX. Several PDA-associated pathways (cell cycle, stress response, Rho GTPase signaling) and cancer driver hub genes (EGFR, JUN) exhibited a cancer-specific rhythmic pattern intricately linked to the circadian clock. Through the integration of multiple functional measurements for rhythmic cancer driver genes, we identified top chronotherapy targets and validated key findings in molecularly divergent pancreatic cancer cell lines. Testing the chemotherapeutic efficacy of clinically relevant drugs further revealed temporal variations that correlated with drug-target cycling. Collectively, our study unravels the PDA circadian transcriptome and highlights a potential approach for optimizing chrono-chemotherapeutic efficacy.
overall_design: To investigate the circadian transcriptome of 4 pancreatic cancer cell lines and 6 patient derived pancreatic cancer organoids. Temporal RNA-Seq was carried out at 7 time points (0h, 4h, 8h, 12h, 16h, 20h, 24h) and daily changes in gene expression were quanitifed at the transcriptome-wide level.

title: ASPC1_0h
source_name_ch1: Pancreatic cancer cell line
characteristics_ch1: cell type: Pancreatic cancer cell line
treatment_protocol_ch1: Human pancreatic cell line AsPC-1 (ATCC Cat# CRL-1682TM) was cultured in Roswell Park Memorial Institute medium (RPMI-1640 ATCC Cat# 30-2001), PANC-1 (ATCC Cat# CRL-1469TM) and MIA PaCa-2 1 (ATCC Cat# CRL-1420TM) were cultured in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle's Medium (DMEM), Capan-1 (ATCC Cat# HTB-79TM) was cultured in Iscove's Modified Dulbecco's Medium (IMDM) Cat# 30-2005TM. All the cell culture media were supplemented with 10% FBS (except 20% for IMDM), and 1% penicillin-streptomycin, and cells were incubated in a humidified incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
growth_protocol_ch1: Pancreas cancer tissue was collected from untreated patients undergoing tissue biopsy at Rush University Medical Center. Immediately following the tissue acquisition, the samples were processed as previously described. Briefly, after digestion with collagenase-II, dispase-II, and DNase-I, biopsy tissues were washed several times and then plated in 50 µL Matrigel domes on a 24-welled plate supplemented with 500 µL organoid medium.
extract_protocol_ch1: For RNA extraction, cells and organoids were cultured in a 6-well plate followed by dexamethasone treatment. 24 h after the synchronization, cells were collected and lysed with RLT buffer containing 1% 2-mercaptoethanol (Bio-Rad, CA). According to the instructions, RNA was isolated using RNeasy® extraction kit (Qiagen, Germany).

RNA concentration was measured using a NanoDrop 2000c spectrophotometer (Thermo Scientific, MA). cDNA was prepared from the purified RNA using a cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit (Applied Biosystems, United States).
data_processing: Reads from the RNA-Sequencing data were aligned to the Homo Sapiens genome assembly GRCh38 (mm10) using the STAR software
Duplicated aligned reads were marked and removed using the Picardtools software
The gene expression count data were extracted using the HTseq software
The raw count data were normalized, followed by log2 transformation. We filtered out genes with mean read counts < 6. All data preprocessing was performed using R software.
Assembly: hg38
Supplementary files format and content: tab-delimited txt files with feature counts per gene

extract_protocol_ch1: For RNA extraction, cells and organoids were cultured in a 6-well plate followed by dexamethasone treatment. 24 h after the synchronization, cells were collected and lysed with RLT buffer containing 1% 2-mercaptoethanol (Bio-Rad, CA). cell type: Patient derived organoids of pancreatic cancer
treatment_protocol_ch1: Human pancreatic cell line AsPC-1 (ATCC Cat# CRL-1682TM) was cultured in Roswell Park Memorial Institute medium (RPMI-1640 ATCC Cat# 30-2001), PANC-1 (ATCC Cat# CRL-1469TM) and MIA PaCa-2 1 (ATCC Cat# CRL-1420TM) were cultured in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle's Medium (DMEM), Capan-1 (ATCC Cat# HTB-79TM) was cultured in Iscove's Modified Dulbecco's Medium (IMDM) Cat# 30-2005TM. All the cell culture media were supplemented with 10% FBS (except 20% for IMDM), and 1% penicillin-streptomycin, and cells were incubated in a humidified incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
growth_protocol_ch1: Pancreas cancer tissue was collected from untreated patients undergoing tissue biopsy at Rush University Medical Center. Immediately following the tissue acquisition, the samples were processed as previously described. Briefly, after digestion with collagenase-II, dispase-II, and DNase-I, biopsy tissues were washed several times and then plated in 50 µL Matrigel domes on a 24-welled plate supplemented with 500 µL organoid medium.
extract_protocol_ch1: For RNA extraction, cells and organoids were cultured in a 6-well plate followed by dexamethasone treatment. 24 h after the synchronization, cells were collected and lysed with RLT buffer containing 1% 2-mercaptoethanol (Bio-Rad, CA). According to the instructions, RNA was isolated using RNeasy® extraction kit (Qiagen, Germany).

RNA concentration was measured using a NanoDrop 2000c spectrophotometer (Thermo Scientific, MA). cDNA was prepared from the purified RNA using a cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit (Applied Biosystems, United States).
data_processing: Reads from the RNA-Sequencing data were aligned to the Homo Sapiens genome assembly GRCh38 (mm10) using the STAR software
Duplicated aligned reads were marked and removed using the Picardtools software
The gene expression count data were extracted using the HTseq software
The raw count data were normalized, followed by log2 transformation. We filtered out genes with mean read counts < 6. All data preprocessing was performed using R software.
Assembly: hg38
Supplementary files format and content: tab-delimited txt files with feature counts per gene

extract_protocol_ch1: For RNA extraction, cells and organoids were cultured in a 6-well plate followed by dexamethasone treatment. 24 h after the synchronization, cells were collected and lysed with RLT buffer containing 1% 2-mercaptoethanol (Bio-Rad, CA). According to the instructions, RNA was isolated using RNeasy® extraction kit (Qiagen, Germany).

RNA concentration was measured using a NanoDrop 2000c spectrophotometer (Thermo Scientific, MA). cDNA was prepared from the purified RNA using a cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit (Applied Biosystems, United States).
data_processing: Reads from the RNA-Sequencing data were aligned to the Homo Sapiens genome assembly GRCh38 (mm10) using the STAR software
Duplicated aligned reads were marked and removed using the Picardtools software
The gene expression count data were extracted using the HTseq software
The raw count data were normalized, followed by log2 transformation. We filtered out genes with mean read counts < 6. All data preprocessing was performed using R software.
